A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SteerEval research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered prompt appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original steering experiments on three language models, including benchmark scores in Tables 2 and 7–10, sensitivity analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds human-validation results for the evaluator and dataset in Appendix D and Table 11.

M1.justification: The benchmark hierarchy, synthesis pipeline, steering procedures, and generation/evaluation prompts remain unchanged. v1 Appendices D/E become v2 Appendices E/F. Additional human-review documentation does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Language Features, Personality, Sentiment, and the appendix Reasoning Patterns domain across L1–L3. The new human checks sample existing data and generations without adding task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Vanilla, Prompt (0-shot), Prompt (3-shot), PCA, DiffMean, and RePS on the same three model backbones. No steering comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a human-validation protocol using 432 sampled generations across concepts and baselines, assessing Concept Score agreement by granularity. Existing benchmark splits, model configurations, steering-factor selection, and GPT-4.1-mini scoring remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D substantially extends validation by testing human–judge alignment and quantifying synthetic-data validity. v1 described manual quality control without reporting these quantitative checks. The existing few-shot, steering-strength, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 first reports statistical agreement estimates: Spearman and Pearson correlations, quadratic weighted kappa for human–judge alignment, and Cohen's kappa for dataset annotation. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing steering scores and findings remain unchanged. New Table 11 reports overall Spearman/Pearson/QWK values of 0.86/0.87/0.87, with strongest agreement at L3. Appendix D.2 adds a 94.1% dataset pass rate and Cohen's kappa of 0.82.

T1.justification: The steering formulation in Equation 1 and the L1–L3 definitions are retained. The new empirical agreement measures introduce no mathematical derivations, formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a hierarchical steering benchmark and evidence of control degrading under finer specifications. The validation appendix supplies support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes stronger L3 human–judge agreement to clearer, less ambiguous concepts and interprets the validation outcomes as supporting evaluator and dataset reliability. The original limitations concerning LLM-judge bias remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct SteerEval documentation link and details concept-review criteria, unanimous retention, and binary labeling for a 20% dataset audit. Existing hardware, steering-layer settings, hyperparameters, and prompt templates are retained; the added details do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds Azaria et al. (2024), Huajun Chen (2024), and Luo et al. (2025) as supporting references in the introduction and evaluation discussion. Positioning relative to AXBENCH, STEER-BENCH, and existing steering methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgements and a two-subsection validation appendix, renumbers the retained prompt appendices, and updates an author affiliation. The existing narrative and section organization otherwise receive limited editing.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11, adjusts caption styling, including colored best/second-best labels in Table 2, and relocates retained appendix tables as prompt boxes reflow. Existing figure artwork and original table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked reported human–judge validation and quantitative dataset-quality outcomes. Appendix D and Table 11 provide useful evidence supporting those aspects of reliability. The improvement is bounded: human validation explicitly covers Concept Score, while annotation details remain brief and uncertainty estimates are absent.
